story.title: Trump Urges Ukraine to Cease Strikes on Russian Diesel Refineries Amid Global Shortage
story.summary: Trump has called on Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian diesel refineries, attributing the ongoing global diesel shortage and rising fuel prices to these strikes. He linked the crisis to the broader context of Russia's war rather than U.S. actions.

timeline_highlights.title: Brother of NYPD Officer Who Died from 9/11-Related Cancer Advocates for Victims
timeline_highlights.summary: As the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks approaches, Phil Alvarez, a retired NYPD detective, reflects on his brother Luis's death from cancer linked to toxins at Ground Zero. Alvarez is working to extend the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund to assist others affected by similar health issues. This year, a seventh moment of silence will be observed to honor those who have died from illnesses related to the toxic dust from the attacks.

event_overview.title: About 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.subject: 9/11 Victim Compensation
event_overview.summary: The September 11th Victim Compensation Fund (VCF) is a federally funded, no-fault compensation program for people who suffered eligible physical harm or died as a result of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks or related debris-removal work. It is distinct from the World Trade Center Health Program: the VCF provides financial compensation, while the health program provides monitoring and treatment for certified conditions.

facts.label: Origins and duration
facts.value: Congress created the original fund in 2001; it operated from 2001 to 2004. The James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act reactivated it in 2011, and the 2019 permanent-authorization law set an October 1, 2090 claim-filing deadline and provides funding necessary for approved claims.

facts.label: Purpose and legal scope
facts.value: The VCF compensates eligible individuals, or personal representatives of those who died, for physical injury, illness, or death connected to the September 11 attacks or immediate post-attack debris removal; it is designed as an alternative to tort litigation.

facts.label: Covered locations and periods
facts.value: For presence eligibility, the program recognizes the World Trade Center and surrounding New York City Exposure Zone from September 11, 2001 through May 30, 2002; the Pentagon site through November 19, 2001; and the Shanksville, Pennsylvania site through October 3, 2001.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The fund is administered by the U.S. Department of Justice, with a Special Master appointed by the Attorney General and operational support from DOJ's Civil Division.

facts.label: Relationship to health benefits
facts.value: VCF eligibility generally requires an eligible physical health condition and proof of presence; World Trade Center Health Program certification is accepted as proof of an eligible condition subject to other requirements. Enrollment in the health program does not automatically register someone with the VCF.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers anniversary-related advocacy and commemoration connected to 9/11 victims; it does not attempt to track every VCF claim, award, health-program development, or related lawsuit.

explore_lenses.label: What changed in the refinery campaign?
explore_lenses.title: Ukraine struck refinery-linked sites as attacks escalated
explore_lenses.summary: Trump's appeal followed another night of long-range Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, while Russia continued large drone and missile attacks on Ukraine. Ukraine portrays refinery strikes as a way to reduce the resources and logistics available to Russia's military.

claims.text: The Associated Press reported that Ukraine's military intelligence agency said its drones hit a processing unit and tank farm at the Slavyansk-on-Kuban refinery; Krasnodar authorities said an industrial site was struck, three people were injured and an oil pipeline was damaged.
Ukraine's Defense Ministry previously identified the Slavyansk ECO refinery as a facility that earns foreign currency and supports Russian logistics in the Azov-Black Sea region.

AP reported that Russia said it downed 389 Ukrainian drones overnight, while Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 453 drones and it neutralized 409; these battlefield claims come from the opposing militaries and were not independently verified in that report.

explore_lenses.label: Are Ukrainian strikes the main cause of diesel prices?
explore_lenses.title: The IEA identifies two major supply shocks
explore_lenses.summary: Ukrainian strikes and Russia's resulting export disruption are contributing to diesel-market tightness, but the IEA attributes the squeeze to a larger combined shock involving severely constrained Gulf exports and refinery disruption in Russia.

claims.text: The IEA said combined net diesel/gasoil exports from the Gulf and Russia were 1.6 million barrels per day lower in August than in February; together, those suppliers had represented almost 45% of global seaborne diesel/gasoil trade in February.

The IEA said Gulf diesel/gasoil exports averaged 390,000 barrels per day in August—just over one-quarter of pre-war levels—as Strait of Hormuz flows remained constrained; it said disruption to Russia's refining system and a near-halt in product exports after intensified Ukrainian attacks compounded those losses.

Trump said Ukraine should stop hitting Russian diesel facilities because the strikes were harming the world; Kyiv's stated rationale, as reported by AP, is that Russia's oil sector both finances and directly fuels its invasion.

Forecast: The IEA projects world oil supply will average 100.7 million barrels per day in 2026 and says a full recovery of Middle East producer supply is deferred until 2027, contingent on the conflict and shipping disruption easing.

explore_lenses.label: What diplomatic or operational steps are next?
explore_lenses.title: No refinery pause or peace meeting was confirmed
explore_lenses.summary: Trump said he had raised the refinery issue with Zelenskyy, but the reporting consulted did not establish that Ukraine accepted a halt. Separately, Moscow signaled openness to renewed three-way talks, without announcing a date, venue or agreed agenda.

claims.text: Trump said he had spoken with Zelenskyy and urged him to stop strikes on Russian diesel infrastructure, but neither AP nor ABC News reported an announced Ukrainian commitment to do so.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia did not rule out Russia-Ukraine-US talks resuming in October, according to AP; this was an expression of openness rather than a confirmed meeting.
AP reported that Russia and Ukraine continued exchanging major drone strikes on September 13, including Ukrainian strikes on refinery-related targets and Russian attacks on Odesa and western Ukraine.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump said he urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop strikes on Russian diesel facilities, arguing that the attacks were worsening a global diesel shortage and rising fuel prices. No Ukrainian commitment to halt the strikes was reported. The appeal follows continued large-scale drone exchanges, including Ukrainian attacks on refinery-related targets and Russian strikes on Odesa and western Ukraine.

sections.heading: Diesel Supply Losses Have Multiple Causes
sections.body: The International Energy Agency said combined net diesel and gasoil exports from the Gulf and Russia were 1.6 million barrels per day lower in August than in February. Gulf exports averaged 390,000 barrels per day, just over one-quarter of pre-war levels, with Strait of Hormuz flows still constrained. The agency said disruption to Russia's refining system and a near-halt in product exports after intensified Ukrainian attacks compounded the losses, but the evidence does not establish the strikes' precise share of the price increase.

sections.heading: Ukraine Cites Russia's War Logistics
sections.body: Kyiv has portrayed refinery strikes as attacks on infrastructure that finances and directly supports Russia's invasion. Ukraine's Defense Ministry previously described the Slavyansk ECO refinery as a source of foreign currency and logistical support for Russian forces in the Azov-Black Sea region. AP reported that Ukrainian military intelligence said drones struck a processing unit and tank farm at Slavyansk-on-Kuban, while Krasnodar authorities said an industrial site was hit, injuring three people and damaging an oil pipeline.

sections.heading: Diplomatic Talks Remain Unscheduled
sections.body: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Russia did not rule out Russia-Ukraine-US talks resuming in October, an expression of openness rather than confirmation of a meeting. The IEA forecasts world oil supply will average 100.7 million barrels per day in 2026 and says a full recovery of Middle East producer supply is deferred until 2027, contingent on easing conflict and shipping disruption.

related_stories.title: EU Leaders Convene in Finland to Discuss Arctic Policy Amid Security Concerns
related_stories.summary: European leaders are gathering in Finland to address key issues related to the Arctic, including shipping routes, resource management, and security challenges posed by the increasing presence of Russia. The meeting comes as the region becomes more accessible due to melting ice, raising concerns about geopolitical tensions involving the US, China, and Russia.
